title: Privacy
lead: What minelog hides, what it stores for {days} days, and what it never collects.

sections.heading: What gets hidden
paragraphs: Before your log is uploaded, minelog replaces IP addresses, MAC addresses, user folder names, access tokens and email addresses. The switch next to Get link turns this on and off. With it off, the log is saved exactly as you pasted it.
It happens twice: once in your browser, so the preview shows what will be saved, and again on our server before anything is stored. Skipping the browser step doesn't get around it.
Two things it doesn't cover. Player names stay in on purpose, since you need them to debug. IPv6 addresses aren't hidden yet, so look for them before you share.

sections.heading: What we store
paragraphs: Each log is saved with its text, the type we detected, its line count, error and warning counts, whether hiding was on, when it expires, and which app uploaded it if the app said so. If hiding was off, the log page says so.
To limit uploads we keep a keyed hash of your IP address, and you can save {uploads} logs a minute and {perDay} a day. We never store the address itself.
Every log is deleted {days} days after it's saved, and its link stops working.

The person who saves a log can delete it themselves during the first hour. To make that possible, saving hands your browser a secret delete token, and we keep only a hash of it, never the token. It stays in your browser storage for that hour and is not sent anywhere else.

sections.heading: What we don't collect
paragraphs: No accounts. A log page sets no cookies and loads nothing from anyone else: your browser only talks to minelog, and the fonts and icons come from our own server. Log addresses are never sent to any analytics service.

The home page, the guides, the API docs and this page do use Google Analytics, to count visits and see which pages people read. Google Analytics sets cookies on those pages. It sees the page, roughly where you are and your device type, and never anything from a log. It doesn't run at all for visitors in the European Union, the wider European Economic Area, the United Kingdom or Switzerland, because it would need your consent first. We work out where you are from your connection when the page loads, and we don't store it.
The other exception is the Ask AI button. When you click it, it opens Claude or ChatGPT with the error lines from your log in the question. Nothing is sent unless you click.

sections.heading: Who can see a log
paragraphs: Every log gets a random 9-character link that nobody can guess. There's no password, so anyone with the link can read the log and its raw text. Only share it with people you trust.

If you share a log by mistake, you can delete it yourself in the first hour, from the button at the bottom of its page. That button only shows in the browser that saved the log. After that hour the log stays readable until it expires, so check the preview first.

README pages show the pictures the README points to, loaded straight from the sites that host them, so those sites can see your IP address. minelog checks the pictures in your browser and removes any that look like adult content. Nothing is sent to us or to anyone else for that. It can only check pictures the host lets it read, and no check is perfect.
